title: Time, Speed and Distance

steps.title: The three-variable relationship
steps.content: Distance, speed and time are linked: distance = speed × time. Rearrange to find speed or time. Keep units consistent before calculating.
steps.formula:
Distance = Speed × Time
Speed = Distance ÷ Time
Time = Distance ÷ Speed
steps.example: A car travels at 60 km/h for 2.5 hours. Distance = 60×2.5 = 150 km.

steps.title: Find the distance
steps.prompt: A bus travels at 45 km/h for 4 hours. How far does it travel?

steps.title: Convert units
steps.content: To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5. Convert minutes to hours when speed is in km/h.

steps.title: Convert speed
steps.prompt: Convert 54 km/h into metres per second.

steps.title: Relative speed
steps.content: When two objects move in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of their speeds. When they move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference.
steps.example: Two trains at 50 and 40 km/h in opposite directions approach each other at 90 km/h.

questions.prompt: A 150 km trip takes 3 hours. Find average speed.
A train moves at 72 km/h. How far does it travel in 25 minutes?
Two cars travel in opposite directions at 55 and 65 km/h. Relative speed is:
A 120 m train crosses a pole in 6 seconds. Find its speed.
questions.explanation: Distance = train length = 120 m. Speed = 120/6 = 20 m/s.

learning_objectives: Use speed, distance and time relationships.
Interpret average speed over multiple legs.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Average speed is always the average of two speeds.
common_misconceptions.correction: Average speed is total distance divided by total time.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Opposite-direction relative speed is the difference.
common_misconceptions.correction: For opposite directions, add speeds; for same direction, subtract.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Minutes and hours can be mixed without conversion.
common_misconceptions.correction: Convert units before substituting into formulas.

worked_examples.title: Find distance
worked_examples.explanation: Use consistent units for speed and time.

worked_examples.title: Relative speed
worked_examples.input: Two cars move toward each other at 40 and 50 km/h
worked_examples.explanation: Add speeds when objects move toward each other.

worked_examples.title: Average speed
worked_examples.input: Travel 60 km at 30 km/h and 60 km at 60 km/h
trace: Total distance 120 km; total time 3 hours.
worked_examples.explanation: Average speed is total distance divided by total time, not the simple mean of speeds.

company_applications.practice: Convert units and calculate relative speed.
Use total distance over total time for averages.
Draw a timeline for trains and meeting problems.

srs_cards.question: What are the key ideas in Time, Speed and Distance?
srs_cards.answer: Use speed, distance and time relationships. Convert units consistently. Solve relative-speed problems. Interpret average speed over multiple legs.

srs_cards.question: Name a common mistake in Time, Speed and Distance.
srs_cards.answer: Average speed is total distance divided by total time.
